=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:899-1055 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The ref branch in scan_content_line stores a `Line or code reference:` range such as `lines 1020-1060` as two point anchors, 1020 and 1060, and process_block only checks `anc_line[s, k] >= lo - tolerance && anc_line[s, k] <= hi + tolerance`, so a reviewer range that contains the consolidated LINES (e.g. `1030-1045`, window 1027-1048) never counts as support.
  WHY: The reviewer who cited the wider range is not counted, so `cnt` drops to 1, below `REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_MIN` (2), and from round 3 a finding raised by two reviewers becomes `advisory-lone` and the round can log `outcome=approve`; this contradicts the "A stray number can only add support" comment, and the fix is to store range anchors and test for overlap with `anc_lo <= hi + tolerance && anc_hi >= lo - tolerance` (gemini stated no severity; all others MAJOR).
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:914-935 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The panel-size guard in prepare() (`if (sec_nonempty[s]) { panel++ }`) counts every non-empty reviewer section, including a failed reviewer's one-line failure message, because scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh writes `Reviewer ${model} failed after ...` to the output file and scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh bundles every `review_*.txt` file without checking its status.
  WHY: With three slots, two successes and one failure, `panel=3`, so `panel < min_reviewers + 1` is false and the rule applies, letting a finding from one of only two working reviewers be demoted to advisory; this breaks the rule that with fewer than `REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_MIN_REVIEWERS + 1` reviewers in the round the rule does not apply (gemini stated no severity; all others MAJOR).
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:899-908 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When the `Line or code reference:` label is empty and the reference is on the next line, the ref branch clears `pending_file[s]` without recording an anchor, whereas scripts/review_floor_rules.sh supports this shape through `pending_line_ref` (lines 478-489).
  WHY: A reviewer using this accepted template shape produces no anchor, so unless an EVIDENCE quote of at least 24 characters matches, it is not counted and a finding raised by two reviewers becomes `advisory-lone` from round 3 (gemini stated no severity; all others MAJOR).
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:883-891 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `File:` regex runs on the raw `line` and is anchored with a trailing `[[:space:]]*$`, so a backticked value (`File: \`scripts/x.sh\``) or an annotated value (`File: scripts/x.sh (process_block)`) never sets `pending_file[s]`; scripts/review_floor_rules.sh (lines 450-490) accepts both.
  WHY: Sections in these shapes produce no anchor, so the supporting reviewer is not counted and a consensus finding is demoted to `advisory-lone` from round 3, while the floor-rules parser credits it to both reviewers (all MAJOR; confidence ranges from 3 to 4).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:lines 899-908, in scan_content_line, the `line or code reference|code` branch: `while (nref < 20 && match(ref, /[0-9]+/)) { add_anchor(s, pending_file[s], substr(ref, RSTART, RLENGTH)) ... }`. The matching check is in process_block: `anc_line[s, k] >= lo - tolerance && anc_line[s, k] <= hi + tolerance`. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A reference range such as `Line or code reference: lines 1020-1060` is stored as two point anchors, 1020 and 1060, so they miss a narrowed `LINES: 1030-1045` (window 1027-1048), and the two ranges are never checked for overlap.
  WHY: `cnt` drops to 1, below `REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_MIN` (2), so from round 3 a two-reviewer finding becomes `advisory-lone`, the editor gets only an ADVISORY stub and the round can log `outcome=approve`; the suggested fix is to store `anc_lo`/`anc_hi` and count support when the ranges overlap.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:line 890, `match(line, /^[[:space:]]*[Ff][Ii][Ll][Ee]:[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*)[[:space:]]*$/, f)`, which runs on the raw `line`. Also lines 899-908, where the ref branch sets `pending_file[s] = ""` even when the reference has no number. For comparison, scripts/review_floor_rules.sh lines 450-490 handle `pending_file` and `pending_line_ref`. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The parser accepts fewer shapes than review_floor_rules.sh: (a) a backticked `File:` value, (b) an annotated `File:` value with trailing text, and (c) an empty `Line or code reference:` label with the reference on the next line, which clears `pending_file` (floor rules handles (c) through `pending_line_ref` at lines 478-489).
  WHY: These shapes produce no anchor, so `cnt` stays at 1 and the finding becomes `advisory-lone` from round 3 while floor rules credits both reviewers; the suggested fix is to strip backticks and quotes, drop the `$` anchor, and keep a pending-ref flag.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:prepare(), from line 914: `for (s = 1; s <= nsec; s++) { if (sec_nonempty[s]) { panel++ } }` and `else if (panel < min_reviewers + 1) { reason = "panel_too_small" }`. Related code: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh lines 902-923 bundles every `review_*.txt` file without checking its status, and scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh lines 5507 and 5519-5520 write `Reviewer ${model} failed after ...` into the failed reviewer's `${output_file}`. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The panel-size guard counts a failed reviewer's non-empty failure message as a participating reviewer.
  WHY: With 3 configured reviewers and 1 failure, `panel` is 3 and the rule applies (`reason=applied`), against the issue's "fewer than `REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_MIN_REVIEWERS + 1`" rule; the suggested fix is to exclude sections matching `^Reviewer .* failed after ` or to skip files whose status is `failed`.

  Requirement: "A lone finding below that bar is written to the ledger as advisory, shown in the PR's review comment under its own heading, and passed to the review-blocked judge. It is never dropped silently."

- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:process_block (around line 986) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The range anchor check tests whether an anchor falls inside the line range rather than whether the ranges overlap.
  WHY: A reviewer citing lines 1020-1060 for a finding at 1030-1045 is ignored because neither endpoint falls within the range +/- tolerance, so reviewers are undercounted and findings are wrongly demoted to `advisory-lone`.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:prepare (around line 935) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The panel-size guard counts every non-empty reviewer section, including error and failure messages, as a participating reviewer.
  WHY: A failed run inflates the panel size, so the convergence rule applies when fewer than `min_reviewers + 1` successful reviews occurred.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:scan_content_line (around line 906) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `Line or code reference:` branch expects the reference on the same line and clears `pending_file` immediately, so it cannot anchor a reference on the next line as scripts/review_floor_rules.sh does.
  WHY: Reviewers using the standard template lose their support anchors, so reviewers are undercounted and findings are wrongly demoted to `advisory-lone`.
